title: Oil, propane or electric heat, plus AC? A national model says 95 to 100 percent of homes save.
question: Does a heat pump always beat oil, propane and electric baseboard heat on running cost?
alternates: Leaving Oil or Propane? What a Heat Pump Saves
The Homes Where Heat Pumps Save the Most
premise: Against propane and electric resistance heat the evidence is consistent: NREL's model gives lower bills for 95-100% of such homes with AC, Minnesota field tests measured savings of about a third against propane and half against resistance heat, and metered New England mini-splits beat both at every observed temperature. Oil is the exception: the New England meters show heat pumps were cheaper than oil only above a break-even of about 12 to 32F depending on the year's oil price, and Deetjen finds oil-heated homes usually take a private loss over the equipment's life once capital is counted, mostly because they sit in cold climates, while resistance and propane homes usually gain; RMI finds the greatest immediate cost benefit for oil and propane customers, and LBNL's project data find the largest bill cuts most likely in propane and oil homes. In the UK, households that left electric heating used less electricity after installing a heat pump. The field studies are small samples; the national models are models.
whyWatch: The gas debate gets the attention, but millions of homes burn oil or propane or use baseboard heaters, and for them the evidence points much more clearly one way, with one exception worth knowing.
tension: Advocates say a heat pump beats every expensive fuel. The meters agree for propane and resistance heat; oil depends on the price and the temperature.

arc.hook: If you heat with propane, oil or baseboards, your heating bill may be twice your neighbour's on gas.
arc.conflict: A heat pump should win easily against expensive fuels, but oil prices swing and cold snaps narrow the gap.
arc.evidence: Bill-saving shares from the national model, measured savings in Minnesota, and the oil break-even temperatures from New England meters.
arc.resolution: Against propane and resistance heat a heat pump wins almost everywhere; against oil it wins most of the season, with the margin set by oil prices.
arc.takeaway: If you heat with propane or baseboards, a heat pump is very likely to cut your costs; with oil, check the break-even and the installed price.

evidence.by: Wilson 2024 (NREL and LBNL), heat pumps for all?
evidence.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see lower bills in 95-100% of cases (median $300-$650/yr); 73-86% without AC; still 87-99% (propane) and 66-100% (oil) at 2019 prices.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: Edwards 2024, inequities in heat pump bill savings
evidence.note: In Edwards' county model, where homes heat with electricity (resistance) or non-gas fuels, heating is generally more expensive and heat pump bill savings are higher.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: RMI 2018, the economics of electrifying buildings
evidence.note: In Providence, RMI's heat pumps have a lower 15-year net present cost than both oil and propane systems, and save at least $10,000 against propane.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: CEE 2018, ducted and ductless cold-climate heat pumps in the field
evidence.note: Measured cost savings averaged 33% against propane furnaces and 53% against electric resistance in Minnesota homes; oil was not tested, so the claim is supported for two of its three fuels.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: Cadmus 2016, ductless mini-split evaluation (MA and RI)
evidence.note: Mini-splits were cheaper to run than electric resistance and propane at all observed temperatures, but against oil they were cheaper only above a price-dependent break-even (about 32 F in 2016, 12 F in 2015).
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: Bernard 2024 (NBER), UK heat pumps and a time-of-use tariff
evidence.note: In the UK, households previously on electric heating used less electricity after a heat pump, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not tested.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

evidence.by: Canadian Climate Institute 2023, heat pumps pay off
evidence.note: Heat pumps use up to 65% less energy than electric baseboards, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not modelled.
evidence.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

audit.text: A heat pump costs less to run than heating with oil, propane or electric resistance
limitations: CEE 2018, ducted and ductless cold-climate heat pumps in the field: Measured cost savings averaged 33% against propane furnaces and 53% against electric resistance in Minnesota homes; oil was not tested, so the claim is supported for two of its three fuels.

Cadmus 2016, ductless mini-split evaluation (MA and RI): Mini-splits were cheaper to run than electric resistance and propane at all observed temperatures, but against oil they were cheaper only above a price-dependent break-even (about 32 F in 2016, 12 F in 2015).

Bernard 2024 (NBER), UK heat pumps and a time-of-use tariff: In the UK, households previously on electric heating used less electricity after a heat pump, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not tested.
Canadian Climate Institute 2023, heat pumps pay off: Heat pumps use up to 65% less energy than electric baseboards, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not modelled.

short.hook: Oil, propane or electric heat, plus AC? A national model says 95 to 100 percent of homes save.
carries: a modelled estimate of what bills would be, not measured bills, and only for homes that already have air conditioning; without AC the same model says only 73 to 86 percent come out ahead
the $300 to $650 median saving is for those same homes: heating mainly with electricity, fuel oil or propane, with air conditioning, and it moves with the heat pump's efficiency
